data.title: China XLX Reports Successful Commissioning of Xinjiang Project Phase I

data.title: Hua Medicine Reports U.S. Phase 1b Results for HMS1005
data.description:
The latest update is out from Hua Medicine ( (HK:2552) ).

Hua Medicine reported topline results from a U.S. Phase 1b multiple ascending dose study of HMS1005 in 48 adults with Type 2 diabetes. Across once-daily doses of 123 mg to 492 mg, HMS1005 was generally well tolerated, with no serious adverse events or severe hypoglycemia reported.

Over the 14-day treatment period, continuous glucose monitoring showed improved glucose management. At drug-tolerant doses of 123 mg to 369 mg, time in range increased and the glucose management indicator decreased, while dorzagliatin has been prescribed to more than 600,000 patients in mainland China.

data.title: HUTCHMED Initiates Phase III Ranosidenib Trial in China
data.description:
An announcement from HUTCHMED (China) ( (HK:0013) ) is now available.

HUTCHMED (China) is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering, developing and commercializing targeted therapies and immunotherapies for cancer and immunological diseases. It has five medicines marketed in China, with its first also approved in the United States, Europe and Japan.

HUTCHMED has initiated RANOVA, a registrational Phase III trial in China evaluating oral ranosidenib against placebo in patients with postoperative residual or recurrent Grade 2 glioma carrying IDH1 or IDH2 mutations; the first patient was dosed on November 20, 2026. The study plans to enroll approximately 210 patients and will assess progression-free survival alongside safety, quality of life and overall survival, while HUTCHMED retains worldwide rights to the dual IDH1/IDH2 inhibitor.

data.title: KJ103 Receives U.S. FDA Orphan Drug Designation for GBS
data.description:
Shanghai Bao Pharmaceuticals Co Ltd Class H ( (HK:2659) ) has issued an announcement.

Shanghai Bao Pharmaceuticals is developing KJ103, a recombinant IgG-degrading enzyme for immune-mediated diseases and conditions driven by pathogenic IgG antibodies. Its disclosed development areas include Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) and desensitization therapy for highly sensitized kidney-transplant patients.

The U.S. FDA granted KJ103 Orphan Drug Designation for GBS, the product’s first such U.S. designation, marking what the company describes as an important overseas-development milestone. Under the program, a drug approved for the designated indication may receive seven years of U.S. market exclusivity, clinical-trial tax credits, a Prescription Drug User Fee Act application-fee exemption and specialized FDA guidance; the company initiated a Phase II GBS trial in China in November 2025.

data.title: Jenscare Presents 12-Month LuX-Valve Plus Clinical Follow-Up Results
data.description:
An update from Jenscare Scientific Co. Ltd. Class H ( (HK:9877) ) is now available.

Jenscare Scientific develops the LuX-Valve Plus transvenous tricuspid valve replacement system for patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation at high surgical risk. Its treatment focus includes patients with large annuli, for whom the system provides seven valve sizes accommodating annuli up to 70 mm.

The 12-month EU TRINITY follow-up covered 149 patients at 20 global centers, with more than 75% receiving valve sizes from 55 mm to 70 mm. Reported outcomes included a 96.6% device success rate and average device operation time of 41.6 minutes; among evaluable patients, 80.6% had no more than moderate TR and 92.1% reached NYHA class I/II, while paired-patient KCCQ scores and six-minute walking distance improved by approximately 17 points and 39 meters, respectively.

data.title: Four Seas Mercantile Accepts Ten-Year Premises Lease Offer
data.description:
Four Seas Mercantile Holdings Limited ( (HK:0374) ) has shared an update.

An indirect wholly owned subsidiary accepted the lessor’s offer on 20 November 2026 to rent premises for 10 years, with a stated commencement date of 15 February 2027 or another date specified by the lessor, and an option to renew for a further five years subject to approval. The accepted offer forms a legally binding contract until superseded by the lease, and the subsidiary must execute the lease and admission application within one month after receiving the relevant documents.

Under HKFRS 16, the Group will recognise a right-of-use asset with an unaudited value estimated at approximately HK$377 million, subject to final audit. Because the applicable percentage ratios exceed 25% but remain below 100%, the transaction is classified as a major transaction under the Listing Rules; written approval from shareholders holding approximately 56.81% of the company was accepted in lieu of a general meeting.

data.title: Stock Exchange Decision Cites Rule 13.24 Failure and Trading Suspension
data.description:
China Tian Yuan Healthcare Group Limited ( (HK:0557) ) has provided an update.

China Tian Yuan Healthcare Group Limited operates healthcare-related businesses including medical examination, health management, trademark licensing and skincare-products distribution, alongside money lending; it previously operated plastic surgery and light medical beauty services.

The Stock Exchange decided the Company had failed to maintain sufficient operations and assets to warrant continued listing under Rule 13.24, with trading in its shares to be suspended under Rule 6.01(3). The decision followed revenue falling from HK$94.6 million in 2021 to HK$19.8 million in 2025 and losses in each of those five years. The Exchange also considered the remaining and newly acquired businesses limited in scale, with short operating track records and insufficient evidence of viability and sustainability.
